editorial_thesis: The next practical layer of agent leverage is governable memory, attributable identity, and resilient private infrastructure—not more autonomy by default.

topic_groups.title: Agent Memory That Can Be Governed
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fills a neglected coverage gap with fresh work on holistic evaluation, sidecar scheduling, and point-of-use utility.

sources.title: HEAMS: Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems
sources.why_selected: Evaluates performance, efficiency, privacy, sovereignty, and security separately.
sources.usefulness: Provides an acceptance-test shape for persistent Buildn memory.

sources.title: HEAMS code
sources.why_selected: Makes the evaluation framework actionable rather than purely conceptual.

sources.title: Who Schedules Agent Memory? A Sidecar Approach to Long-Horizon Tasks
sources.why_selected: Separates retrieval scheduling from the main task agent.
sources.usefulness: Maps to asynchronous, provenance-aware Buildn context delivery.

sources.title: Delivered, Not Used: Evaluating Agent Memory at Its Point of Use
sources.why_selected: Distinguishes retrieved memories from memories that actually improve decisions.
sources.usefulness: Suggests a missing event type for agent traces.

sources.title: What Is This Memory Useful For? Measuring Task-Conditioned Utility in Long-Term Agent Memory
sources.why_selected: Frames utility as task-conditioned instead of universally beneficial.

topic_groups.title: Agent Identity + Access
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Extends recent runtime-security coverage with a concrete non-human identity lifecycle, current standards work, and a posture scorecard.

sources.title: AI Agent Identity Crisis: Standards Emerge as Enterprises Lag
sources.why_selected: Synthesizes the governance gap around agent discovery, credentials, privilege, and accountability.
sources.usefulness: Direct input to agent registry and revocation design.

sources.title: 2026 State of AI Agent Identity Security report
sources.why_selected: Adds a current industry posture lens based on 400 security and IT leaders.

sources.title: SI Agent Standards Initiative
sources.why_selected: Current NIST work on agent authentication and interoperable security standards.
sources.usefulness: Keeps Buildn principal and delegation models transport-neutral.

topic_groups.title: Developer Infrastructure + Self-Hosting
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Chosen for immediate deployment signal: a GHES release candidate with local security controls plus self-hosting continuity issues that affect real workloads.

sources.title: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 release candidate
sources.why_selected: Adds air-gapped AI secret detection, malicious-package coverage, cooldowns, and expiring OAuth tokens.
sources.usefulness: Candidate for private client staging and policy review.

sources.title: Self-Host Weekly — 20 November 2026
sources.why_selected: Surfaces API monetization, licensing, maintenance, and security changes across self-hosted tools.
sources.usefulness: Supports an upstream dependency continuity ledger.
